title: Annotatio V §.IV FIRST genus (1): merely spiritual food cannot be mouthed corporally — Mt 15:17; stomach/latrine
pass_a_gloss: To the FIRST GENUS of Arguments belongs: (1) That Christ’s Body to be eaten in the Sacred Supper is a merely Spiritual Food, not Corporal — of the Soul alone, not of the Body — destined to be nourishment of the soul only, not also of the Body, even if through this soul-nourishment an exceeding utility also overflows into the Body and so into the whole man, by reason of the closest Union with the soul, to show itself through and after the resurrection from the dead; But a merely spiritual Food cannot be eaten Corporaliter, even as to the Mouth alone — i.e. placed in the Mouth — without by that very act, if it is Food, becoming Corporal Food; and Corporal Food received by the Mouth and not emitted by the same finally goes into the belly, food thus about to become Corporal altogether; Whatever enters into the mouth goes away into the Belly, Matt. 15:17. Food for the Belly and the Belly for foods, 1 Cor. 6:13. The Pontiffs thus far agree that Christ’s Body, transmuted from bread, by the very fact that it is eaten is received not into the mouth alone but also into the belly or stomach. Further, food received in the belly is in part emitted into the privy, according to what else Christ adds in Matt. 15:17: Do you not yet understand that whatever is thrust into the Mouth enters the Belly and is cast out into the latrine. The Pontiffs indeed deny the last consequence and impute it to the Stercoranist heretics — but in vain, seeing it is tied by Christ Himself.
pass_b_english: FIRST genus (1): the Body in the Supper is merely spiritual food for the soul — not corporal food for the body (though soul-nourishment overflows to the whole man after resurrection).

A merely spiritual food cannot be mouthed corporally without becoming corporal food that goes to the belly (Matt. 15:17; 1 Cor. 6:13). Pontiffs agree it reaches the stomach; Christ’s own latrine-clause they vainly shove onto Stercoranists.
source_text: Ad PRIMUM Argumentorum GENUS pertinet. (1) Corpus Christi in Cœna S. manducandum, esse Cibum merè Spiritualem, non Corporalem, solius Animæ, non Corporis, in animæ tantùm, non Corporis etiam alimoniam cessurum, etiamsi per alimoniam hanc animæ, in Corpus quoque, ob arctissimam cum anima Unionem, eóque in totum hominem, utilitas eximia, per & post resurrectionem à mortuis se exsertura, redundet; At Cibus merè spiritualis, Corporaliter, etiam quà Os tantùm, manducari, i. e. Ori imponi, nequit, quin hôc ipsô, si Cibus sit, evadat Cibus Corporalis, Cibus verò Corporalis Ore receptus, nec eôdem emissus, denique abit in ventrem, cibus sic ex toto Corporalis evasurus; Quicquid intrat in os, abit in Ventrem, Matth. 15, 17. Esca Ventri & Venter escis, 1. Cor. 6, 13. Consentiunt hactenus Pontificii, Corpus Christi, ex pane transmutatum, eô ipsô quòd manducatur, non in os tantùm, sed & in ventrem seu stomachum recipi. Porrò ventre receptus cibus, in secessum ex parte emittitur, juxta aliud, quod Matth. 15, 17. additur à Christo: Nondum intelligitis, quicquid intruditur in Os, in Ventrem ingredi & in latrinam ejici. Consequentiam abnuentibus quidem Pontificiis postremam, & Stercoranistis hæreticis imputantibus, sed frustrà, utpote ab ipso Christo nexam.
